'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#D2B1D9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#AE8BB1|50%}} {{legend0|#000000|No data}} | map_size = 300px | title = U.S Senator | before_election = [[Angus King]] | before_party = Independent politician | after_election = [[Angus King]] | after_party = Independent politician }}{{ElectionsME}} The '''2024 United States Senate election in Maine''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] to represent the state of [[Maine]]. Incumbent [[Independent politician|independent]] Senator [[Angus King]] won re-election to a third term, defeating [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee David Costello, [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee Demitroula Kouzounas, and independent Jason Cherry. Primary elections took place on June 11, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=www.ncsl.org}} This election coincided with five referendum questions, including a [[2024 Maine Question 5|referendum to change the state flag]], as well as the [[2024 United States presidential election in Maine|presidential election]], [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Maine|elections]] for the state's two [[Maine's congressional districts|congressional districts]], and various other state, county and local elections. King won re-election to a third term in office with 52.06% of the vote. He outperformed [[Kamala Harris]] in the concurrent presidential election, winning by a margin of 17.42 percentage points to Harris's margin of 6.94 percentage points.
